claims.explanation: Flubendazole is a tubulin-polymerization inhibitor whose selectivity is best explained by mitotic/ microtubule-pathway dependencies rather than by a single lineage. Lines with intact p53 signaling and high proliferative/microtubule gene expression (e.g., high KIF20A/KIF2C/CDC25B, low CDK1/TOP2A/UBE2C after treatment) are more sensitive, whereas EGFR/PIK3CA-driven lines with strong survival signaling and low mitotic dependency are relatively protected. TP53 mutation is common across both groups and is therefore not the primary determinant; instead, p53-pathway competence and mitotic gene expression are the strongest predictors.

features.basis: TP53-mutant lines are enriched among least-affected lines and p53 induction mediates flubendazole antitumor effects (PMID 33197601)
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650) are among least affected, suggesting EGFR survival signaling blunts microtubule-inhibitor killing
PIK3CA-mutant lines appear in both groups but enriched among least-affected, consistent with PI3K-driven survival signaling
Mitotic kinesin upregulated by flubendazole in responsive VCAP cells; high mitotic dependency predicts sensitivity
Mitotic centromere-associated kinesin induced in responsive cells, marking mitotic vulnerability
G2/M regulator induced by flubendazole in responsive cells, indicating reliance on mitotic checkpoints
p21 induction in responsive cells reflects intact p53-pathway response to microtubule stress
MYC downregulation in responsive cells; high MYC-driven proliferation may bypass microtubule dependence
CDK1 is downregulated after treatment in responsive cells, consistent with G2/M arrest as the killing mechanism
Topoisomerase II alpha downregulation in responsive A549 cells marks high proliferation/mitotic index
Ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme downregulated in responsive cells, reflecting mitotic exit dependency
Flubendazole binds tubulin; high TUBB/tubulin expression may increase drug target availability (PMID 20348394)
